statement: Access to personal data is logged, and those logs are reviewed on a defined cycle so unauthorized access is detected, investigated and fixed. The access logs, the related traffic data and the personal data needed to investigate unauthorized access are kept for at least one year, unless another law requires longer. Retention settings on systems are checked against that minimum. Proof is the review records, the alert tickets and the retention settings.
why_asked: Without reviewed access logs a breach of personal data goes unnoticed, and logs deleted too early leave nothing to investigate with.
how_to_ask: Ask who reviews access to personal data, how often and what happened with the last anomaly. Then check how long the logs are kept. Example probe: "Show me the last review of access to customer data and how long those logs are retained."
question: Does your organization review logs of access to personal data so unauthorized access is detected, keeping them for the minimum period it is obliged to?
expected_evidence: Log review records; alert tickets with follow-up; retention settings on logging systems; retention schedule entry for access logs, for the audit period.
good_looks_like: Access to personal data is logged and reviewed on a set cycle, and anomalies are followed up to closure. Logs and related investigation data are kept for at least one year, and system settings match.
test: Sample review cycles from the audit period and check each review took place and anomalies were followed up. Inspect retention settings on logging systems and check the oldest available log. Pass if reviews are evidenced and logs are kept for at least one year.
baseline_risk: Unauthorized access to personal data goes undetected, and the organization cannot investigate or show what happened.
key_settings: dpdpa: keep access logs, traffic data and the personal data needed to investigate unauthorized access for at least one year, unless another law requires longer
